notes:
Replication values are author-derived primary project-table values, not independently converted. Original full primary source unavailable after bounded open-access acquisition. Secondary original values in the replication authors’ workbook were not extracted as primary original evidence. No individual narrative success verdict located; numeric success coding is not treated as narrative.
Source follow-up: Published primary article title, authors, year and DOI verified from supplied text first page. Source version: published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service. Table 8 is the supplied p.20 locator. Requested r is extracted as the explicitly printed uncorrected mean correlation Mr̂; the same row separately prints corrected estimated mean population correlation Mρ̂ = -.23. No conversion performed. Table reports a 95% CI for corrected Mρ̂, but no p value for this association; no p inferred from its confidence interval. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders as required.
Completion source review (es_value_o): Named trait/outcome row in Table 8 matches the supplied description and p.20 locator. Extracted requested uncorrected r as printed in Mr̂ column; the separate corrected M␳ˆ is retained in checkpoint notes.
Completion source review (n_r): Table 1 explicitly lists one test and its replication sample size. No arithmetic or recruitment-total substitution.
Completion source review (es_value_r): Printed observed effect .26, corrected effect .26 retained in notes. Generic printed metric retained; r versus standardized coefficient is not independently distinguishable per row. No metric or sign conversion.
Completion source review (pval_value_r): Explicit two-tailed p < .05 success definition and 100% success for exactly one test establish same-test bound. Exact p not supplied.
Completion source review (reported_success): Authors explicitly label column replication success rate, observed/corrected 100/100. Observed author summary mapped to successful; corrected summary retained in notes. No new significance-based verdict.
